statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits at its low-band floor because every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt, where no Nasdaq-100 price path can form.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON with no danger window. Tail stays far below the block threshold in all 24 published hours. The risk this assessment describes is the size of the repricing gap carried into the Sunday reopen at 22:00Z, roughly eighteen hours past the final slot, rather than anything that can develop inside the window.
headline: A 3.75%-4.00% policy rate, a near-5% 10-year and $100 crude sit out the weekend halt behind a 14.81 VIX, with Tail pinned at its structural floor
body: Every hour in this window falls inside the CME weekend halt. Nasdaq-100 cash settled Friday at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing near the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range. The E-mini NQ last printed 29,917.25, up 0.59%, after opening at 29,723.75 and ranging 29,648.00-29,993.25. VIX fell 4.08% to 14.81 and settled at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range against a 17.71 prior close. The week's anchor was Tuesday's FOMC decision: a unanimous 12-0 vote raising the target range 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00%, the first increase in more than three years, with a dot plot in which 16 of 18 participants expected at least one further move. H.15 shows the 2-year at 4.67% and the 10-year at 4.94% on 17 September, with Friday reporting placing the 10-year near 4.96%. Front-month WTI settled at $100.30, down 1.6%, and Brent at $103.87, with crude still roughly 19% higher over the month after drone damage to Saudi Aramco's East-West pipeline; partial restart is planned within days and full capacity in about six weeks, while Strait of Hormuz shipping risk is unresolved. Friday's tape was dispersed rather than directional: megacaps split four up and four down, semiconductors ranged from ARM +4.04% and MU +3.92% to QCOM -5.82%, and Technology rose 0.84% while Communication Services fell 0.74%. Friday was also the quarterly triple-witching expiry. None of that can produce a path inside the halt, so Tail holds its structural floor at 5 and drifts to 7 by the final slot only to reflect unpriced headline accumulation. The seven-day calendar is unusually light: the BEA schedule places August PCE and the Q2 GDP third estimate on 30 September, beyond the window, leaving the 23 September flash PMIs and Thursday's jobless claims as the significant scheduled checkpoints alongside 2-, 5- and 7-year note auctions.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail ran 15-19 through the European morning and the U.S. cash session, then fell away to 11, 7, 6 and 5 as trading ended and the contract settled, holding 5 across the final five hours. Stress peaked near 51 during the U.S. afternoon before decaying through 33, 28, 27, 26, 25, 24, 23 and 22 into the halt. Confidence held between 82 and 88 throughout. Dominant mode rotated from normal through trend-up during the European morning to mixed across the dispersed U.S. session, then back to normal once the weekend halt began.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed at 20:00Z on Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, roughly eighteen hours after the final slot here. Tail is held between 4 and 7 across the window, with a gradual lift through Saturday evening and the Sunday small hours that reflects the growing stock of unpriced headlines - principally the Middle East supply file - rather than any observed structure. Stress rises slowly from 21 to 26 on the same reasoning, and Confidence decays from 81 to 68 as Friday's verified marks age without a refreshing observation. Dominant mode is normal in every slot and the mapped policy state is unchanged throughout. The genuine sensitivity of this assessment sits beyond its final hour, at the reopen, where a gap that extends without meaningful retracement would be the structure that matters; a gap that is absorbed and retraced would be ordinary.
